title: Is the internet-facing load balancer reachable from the internet?
concluded: Two documents disagree. The client answers say the API gateway is the only public entry; the diagram shows a second, internet-facing load balancer with an arrow from the internet.

sources.quote: The API gateway is the only public entry point

assumed: The load balancer is reachable from the internet and is treated as a second entry point.
would_change: Confirmation that the load balancer accepts traffic only from inside the network.

title: "Key Service" and "signing service" are the same service
concluded: The diagram calls it Key Service and the functional description calls it signing service. The diagram name is kept.

sources.quote: Certificates are signed by the signing service, which uses the CA signing key

would_change: The client saying these are two separate services.

title: The internet-facing load balancer is treated as a second way in
concluded: Requests can reach the certificate service through the internet-facing load balancer without passing the API gateway.

sources.location: page 1, arrow from 'public ALB' to 'internal ALB'

assumed: Nothing on that path checks the sign-in token.
would_change: The certificate service, or the load balancer, checking the sign-in token itself.

review.note: The load balancer only allows the office network.

title: Who can read or delete the audit records is not documented
concluded: The audit trail records API calls in the account, but no document says who can read or delete the records.
would_change: The client naming who has access, or a setting that prevents deletion.
